en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Wood-Ridge, Bergen County, New Jersey, 1917, Sheet 54, part 1 (Passaic Street to North Avenue, Madison Street to 1st Street)
Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Wood-Ridge, Bergen County, New Jersey, 1917, Sheet 54, part 2 (North Avenue to Highland Avenue and Valley Boulevard, 7th Street to Hillcrest Avenue)

sheet-54-1.description: The upper part of sheet 54 covers the southern corner of Wood-Ridge, headed Woodridge on the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch. It runs from Passaic Street, which carries the Carlstadt borough line along its centre, east across Central Avenue, Union Avenue and Main Avenue to North Avenue, and from Madison and 5th Street at the top down to Charter Oak and 1st Street. West of Union Avenue the cross streets are Madison, James, Rose and Charter Oak; east of it they are numbered 5th to 1st Street, meeting Union Avenue with small offsets. The blocks are laid out in narrow house lots, most of them still vacant, with scattered frame dwellings, private auto garages and a few chicken houses. Building is denser east of Union Avenue, between Union and North Avenues. The only works are the S. Hergesell Novelty Works on Passaic Street in block 3, with electric power noted, and a concrete hatchery with frame gables in block 34 near Union Avenue and 4th Street. Water pipes of 6 to 24 inches are drawn in most streets, with fire hydrants at several corners. The north arrow and compass rose stand on the heavy line that divides this part from the lower part of the sheet, which shows the blocks east of North Avenue. Block numbers run from 1 to 4 and 11 to 14 west of Union Avenue and 32 to 36 and 61 to 65 east of it; the margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 50, 55 and 56. Valley Boulevard and Hillcrest Avenue are lettered just beyond North Avenue at the right edge.
notes: Passaic Street is today Fritsch Avenue; it was left out of the control because its drawn width changes at Rose and its junctions with Rose and Charter Oak disagreed with the fit by 7 to 8 m.
Central Avenue is today Center Street.
Madison is today 5th Street and James is today 4th Street between Center Street and Union Avenue.
The 5th Street / North Avenue junction was excluded: the detector paired the east edge of North Avenue with the water pipe.
The sheet heading reads Garfield, N.J.; this sheet belongs to the Garfield volume.

Printed sheet 54 of the Garfield, N.J. volume, headed Woodridge; scale 100 ft to an inch; north about 53 degrees clockwise from up. Two parts at the same rotation, divided by a heavy line: part 1 (top) Passaic St (now Fritsch Avenue, the Carlstadt borough line) to North Av between Madison/5th St and Charter Oak/1st St; part 2 (bottom) North Av to beyond Highland Av between 7th St and Hillcrest Av, with Valley Blvd. Old Central Av is Center Street, Madison is 5th Street and James is 4th Street west of Union Avenue.

sheet-54-2.description: The lower part of sheet 54 shows the blocks of Wood-Ridge immediately east of North Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and set below the heavy line that divides it from the upper part of the sheet. It runs from North Avenue east across Woodridge Avenue, Columbia Boulevard and Highland Avenue to open ground beyond, and from 7th Street at the top down to Hillcrest Avenue at the bottom. The line of 4th Street crosses the part as an 80 foot street with a 24 inch water pipe but no lettered name between North Avenue and Highland Avenue; east of Highland Avenue Valley Boulevard is drawn running diagonally to the right edge. Between 7th and 4th Streets and between 4th Street and Hillcrest Avenue the blocks are long, divided into narrow house lots, with frame dwellings along Woodridge Avenue and Columbia Boulevard and a few private garages; most lots are vacant. East of Highland Avenue the land is almost empty: blocks 98 and 99 carry lot lines only, and the large blocks 102 and 103 are unbuilt, crossed by a dash-dot line marked A and B and by a water pipe along Valley Boulevard. Block numbers are 76 to 78, 84, 85, 88, 89, 98, 99, 102 and 103; the margins refer to sheets 54, 56 and 59. Street names lettered along the left edge (5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd Streets) belong to the cross streets west of North Avenue drawn in the upper part. The sheet scale bar and the Sanborn copyright line of 1917 are at the lower right.
notes: Valley Boulevard today continues west of Highland Avenue along the old 4th Street line to North Avenue.
